scientific_question: Do mule-deer and bighorn GPS night-minus-day relative displacement q vs astronomical daylength differ within the SAME original public Utah source, after selecting their coobserved source-local solar dates with EXACT triple original/even/odd original-collar recording support, using same 43 degree latitude reference as Wyoming, before looking at new Utah cross-taxon date effects?

original_study.rationale: Exactly the same two scientific taxa as the already opened Wyoming original shared-date contrast (source DOI 10.5441/001/1.703), not the stronger or weaker Utah study-native effect selected after viewing shared date results.

prespecified_support_selection.source_preflight: Verify exact source original bitstream UUID, byte count and original MD5, replay ALL FOUR original Utah taxon q and q/daylength source means and eligible original animal counts before any new cross-taxon shared-date effects. Then replay archive source triple original same-tag/date group means for the two preselected taxa to 1e-12. Never rescue weak support by selecting another native pair, changing source years or loosening minimum count thresholds.
prespecified_support_selection.original_three_schedules: Use source-original at most one GPS fix per UTC hour bin with actual accepted 0.5–2h GPS interval; EVEN UTC bin and ODD UTC bin each with accepted actual 1.5–2.5h intervals, original day-night part at interval endpoints/midpoints, min 3 DAY and 3 NIGHT steps on each tag/date/schedule and speed <=60km/h.
prespecified_support_selection.source_tagyear: Within each original individual/calendar-year require >=10 exact original/even/odd daypart-eligible solar dates and common astronomical-daylength span >=0.5h.
prespecified_support_selection.reference_astronomy: Use SAME common fixed 43.0°N reference astronomical photoperiod x from original Wyoming study, not source animal actual latitude or a physical received-sunlight measurement. This removes reference latitude scale variation from source-sign comparison; no weather source queried.
prespecified_support_selection.same_study_calendar_date: Iteratively intersect tag-year solar dates from both native taxa; retain dates on which >=1 source-qualified animal from BOTH taxa had a triple-hour-schedule GPS day; after intersection drop tag-years with <10 shared dates or <0.5h shared reference daylength span, repeat until convergence (max 100). Only SUPPORT, never q values or sign, may enter selection.
prespecified_support_selection.animal_unit: Per source tag equally weight each eligible calendar year and calculate source q/q~L group means and 2000 tagged-animal bootstrap per schedule. Require >=5 original tags in EACH native taxon; otherwise SOURCE_HOLD, not ecological zero.
prespecified_support_selection.month_year_test: For a date-matched average-q difference slope q_mule−q_bighorn vs same x, bootstrap 2000 year-month blocks. Require >=20 coobserved calendar dates, at least 5 original year-month blocks, reference daylength spread>=0.5h; remain null if not supported.
prespecified_support_selection.report: Always publish source DOI and both fixed scientific taxon rows; support counts, native q/q~L coefficients and nominal CIs for ORIGINAL/EVEN/ODD, mule−bighorn contrast and date-level contrast if identifiable; no original GPS tag IDs, true calendar years or days, exact positions/time, per-animal slopes or private GPS track files.

scientific_interpretation: This is a new separate original source DOI from Wyoming but the two taxa were selected after observing Wyoming's positive mule versus negative bighorn result; it is NOT a fully blinded or preregistered external confirmatory replication.

Utah's original GPS acquisition clock is heavily ODD UTC hour biased (roughly 87–96% depending on taxon), and prior strict triple tag support is only ~11 mule-deer and ~45 bighorn; lack of same-calendar support is informative attrition, never a null biological response.
Wyoming shared-date slope was positive mule−negative bighorn on 193 source calendar days, reference latitude 43.0°N. No assumptions of same Utah calendar years, season or shared tags with Wyoming.

A source-signed contrast under this fixed x axis cannot identify causal daylight physiology, thermoregulation, sun navigation, direct heat or general global taxonomic trait effect; habitats, seasons, resources and collars may remain different within and between studies.
Old Movebank source, 12 original ERA5 serialized raw SHA historical HOLDS and 48-source external signed radiation-direction nonreplication are immutable.
Do not use eBird; no TinyFish dependency in source retrieval or execution.
